universalAnswers.whatHappened: OpenAI says it temporarily paused new sign-ups and upgrades to ChatGPT Pro $200, also called Pro 20X, on September 10.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: This is a pause on joining or upgrading into that tier, rather than an automatic cancellation of every active subscription.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: The current OpenAI Help Center policy and a September 11 Computerworld report were reread on September 12.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: OpenAI does not give a restart date in the reviewed policy, and the article makes no capacity or other-product claim.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A reader comparing plans before a busy work period may need to preserve an active Pro $200 subscription or understand why a new upgrade cannot proceed.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: The pause applies to people on Free, Go, Plus or Pro $100 who want to move into Pro $200, while existing Pro $200 subscribers are addressed separately.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Existing Pro $200 subscriptions continue to renew as usual, while Pro $100 remains available for a new upgrade.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: The reviewed sources do not establish when the pause will lift or any individual account outcome outside the stated subscription rules.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Before changing anything, open Settings → My Plan and check your current tier and the next scheduled change.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Am I keeping an active subscription, trying to enter a paused tier, or making a change that could end my current tier?

model-tool-release.productRange: The notice concerns only the ChatGPT Pro $200 / Pro 20X subscription entry and upgrade path, not a general claim about every OpenAI product.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: No new capability is announced; the current change is a temporary restriction on new sign-ups and upgrades into one existing tier.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: The story helps a person decide whether to preserve an active tier or avoid promising a new purchase that the official policy says is unavailable.
model-tool-release.notFor: It is not a release review, a claim about API or business plans, a capacity forecast, or personalized billing advice.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: The reviewed Help Center says Pro $100 remains available for a new upgrade, while account-specific questions remain with the official plan page.
model-tool-release.availability: New Pro $200 sign-ups and upgrades are paused, but existing Pro $200 subscriptions continue to renew as usual.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: The reviewed policy names Free, Go, Plus and Pro $100 as tiers that cannot move into Pro $200 during the pause.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: The story repeats only the named $100 and $200 tier labels and does not infer any price change or future charge.
model-tool-release.limitations: Once Pro $200 ends, OpenAI says it cannot be repurchased until the pause lifts, but it supplies no restart date.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: The explanation uses account state rather than model infrastructure because the reader decision is about a purchase or existing subscription.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: OpenAI owns the current subscription rule; Computerworld corroborates the announced pause without proving a restart date or extra account effect.
